comparatorRouteSelection.route: Dutch-language track — Performing Arts and Creative Technologies
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the Dutch programme title Media en Cultuur, so the Dutch-language track is selected independently of UCR fit. Within that track the target does not name one of four equally formal 30-EC depth packages; the current OER lists Performing Arts and Creative Technologies first, so official order resolves that nested choice. Kunst, cultuur en maatschappij is likewise the first restricted-choice course. The 60-EC profiling space remains open.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option combines film, adaptation, art and cultural analysis. Participatory media adds production, public engagement and environmental communication. The digital option develops AI ethics and hands-on data methods for critical analysis. Each pairing differs by 1/2: 10 courses, 1/3: 13 courses, 2/3: 10 courses. Media heritage could build on media archaeology, documentary, museum studies and art-historical research, much of which is already in the closest option. A performing arts direction could use creative communication, art and audiovisual work, but performance and dance depth is limited. These directions were considered and the maximum of three options is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce film form, history and analysis.
Both examine how media forms and technologies change over time.
Utrecht offers a dedicated new media introduction. UCR examines related topics across media and data courses.
Both analyze television and its cultural role. UCR also studies storytelling and representation on social platforms.
Both study storytelling across cultures and periods. UCR emphasizes myth and literature.
Both examine how art makes meaning. UCR focuses on the history of art interpretation.
Both compare media forms. UCR focuses on adaptation between film and text.
Both consider how exhibitions shape meaning for audiences. UCR emphasizes museum interpretation and curatorial practice.
Utrecht introduces theater and dance as fields of study. UCR includes some performance through creative communication and art.
Both explore creative practice as communication. UCR emphasizes poetic, sonic and performance experiments.
Both study how cultural work engages public issues. UCR focuses on persuasive framing and sustainability communication.
Both develop qualitative research methods. UCR includes interviews, visual methods and thematic analysis.
Utrecht studies the philosophy of science. UCR ethics addresses related questions of responsibility.
Both examine culture in society. UCR takes a broader social-theory approach.
Both develop independent research and critical source use. Utrecht prepares a media and culture thesis. UCR applies these methods to historical inquiry.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and outside the scheduled degree.
Utrecht includes 60 EC of profiling, with at least 30 EC in a coherent package.
